description: The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.

a.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Work out the average number of orders per account, using only accounts that have at least one order. Keep the accounts whose order count is above that average. For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and return only the first 10 rows. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM order_counts), above AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count FROM order_counts oc CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE oc.order_count > o.avg_count), above_avg AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS kept_avg FROM above) SELECT a.account_id, a.order_count, a.order_count - o.avg_count AS diff_from_avg, a.order_count - k.kept_avg AS diff_from_kept_avg FROM above a CROSS JOIN overall o CROSS JOIN above_avg k ORDER BY diff_from_kept_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

c.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Which accounts have more orders than the average number of orders per account? For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of those above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and give only the first 10. Don't round anything. The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.
c.sql:
WITH order_counts AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM `order`
  GROUP BY account_id
),
avg_orders AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM order_counts
),
above AS (
  SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count, oc.order_count - a.avg_count AS diff_from_avg
  FROM order_counts oc
  CROSS JOIN avg_orders a
  WHERE oc.order_count > a.avg_count
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_above
  FROM above
)
SELECT ab.account_id, ab.order_count, ab.diff_from_avg, ab.order_count - aa.avg_above AS diff_from_above_avg
FROM above ab
CROSS JOIN above_avg aa
ORDER BY diff_from_above_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each account_id in the order table, count its rows; take the average of those counts over only the accounts that have at least one order; keep accounts whose count exceeds that average; compute each one's count minus that average and its count minus the mean count of the above-average accounts; sort by the latter descending without rounding; return the top 10 rows as account_id, order count, difference from average, and difference from above-average mean
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), avg_c AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM counts), above AS (SELECT c.account_id, c.order_count FROM counts c, avg_c a WHERE c.order_count > a.avg_count), above_mean AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS above_mean FROM above) SELECT ab.account_id, ab.order_count, ab.order_count - a.avg_count AS diff_from_avg, ab.order_count - m.above_mean AS diff_from_above_mean FROM above ab, avg_c a, above_mean m ORDER BY diff_from_above_mean DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Among accounts that have standing orders (`order.account_id`), count each account's orders. Compute the average number of orders per account using only accounts that have at least one order. Which accounts have an order count above that average? For each one, show the account id, its order count, how far its count exceeds that average, and how far its count exceeds the average order count of only the above-average accounts. Sort by that last difference from largest to smallest, return only the first 10 rows, and don't round any values.
d.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM order_counts), above AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count FROM order_counts oc, avg_all a WHERE oc.order_count > a.avg_count), avg_above AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_above_count FROM above) SELECT ab.account_id, ab.order_count, ab.order_count - a.avg_count AS diff_from_avg, ab.order_count - aa.avg_above_count AS diff_from_above_avg FROM above ab, avg_all a, avg_above aa ORDER BY diff_from_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10;
